questions.title: Count Vowels
questions.prompt: Count how many vowels appear in a given string. Treat uppercase and lowercase vowels the same.
hints: Make every letter lowercase first so A and a are treated the same.
Keep the vowels in a small lookup group: a, e, i, o, u.
Walk through the string one character at a time and add 1 only when the character is a vowel.

visualizer.title: Count Vowels: scan each character
visualizer.caption: Watch the loop check one character at a time and update the vowel count.

questions.title: Reverse Words
questions.prompt: Given a sentence, return the words in reverse order while keeping each word's letters unchanged.
hints: Split the sentence into words.
Reverse the list of words.
Join the reversed words with single spaces.

questions.title: Maximum Score
questions.prompt: Return the largest integer in a list of assignment scores. If the list is empty, return null or the language equivalent.
hints: Handle the empty list first.
Track the best value seen so far.
Compare each score against the current best.

questions.title: Is Palindrome
questions.prompt: Return true if a string reads the same forward and backward after ignoring spaces and case.
constraints: Input may contain spaces and letters.
hints: Normalize case and remove spaces.
Compare characters from both ends.
Stop early if a mismatch appears.

questions.title: Sum Even Numbers
questions.prompt: Given a list of integers, return the sum of only the even numbers.
hints: Start the sum at zero.
Check divisibility by 2.
Add only values that pass the even check.

visualizer.title: Sum Even Numbers: add only the evens
visualizer.caption: Watch each number get checked before the running sum changes.

questions.title: First Repeated Character
questions.prompt: Return the first character that appears more than once while scanning left to right. Return null if none repeat.
hints: Keep a set of seen characters.
Scan left to right.
The first character already in the set is the answer.

questions.title: Grade Bucket
questions.prompt: Convert a numeric score into A, B, C, D, or F using standard 90/80/70/60 cutoffs.
hints: Check highest cutoffs first.
Use if/else branches.
Return once the correct bucket is found.

questions.title: Remove Duplicates Keep Order
questions.prompt: Return a new list with duplicate values removed while preserving the first occurrence order.
hints: Use a set to remember values already copied.
Keep a result list.
Append only when the value has not been seen.

questions.title: Count Words
questions.prompt: Count how many words are in a sentence. Multiple spaces should not create empty words.
hints: Trim or split on whitespace.
Ignore empty pieces.
Return the number of real words.

questions.title: Smallest Positive
questions.prompt: Return the smallest positive integer in a list. Return null if there is no positive integer.
hints: Track a best positive value.
Ignore zero and negative values.
Update the best when a smaller positive appears.

questions.title: Running Total
questions.prompt: Return a list where each position contains the sum of all values up to that position.
hints: Keep a running sum.
Add each number to the running sum.
Append the running sum to the result.

questions.title: Valid Course Code Shape
questions.prompt: Return true if a course code looks like four uppercase letters, optional space, then three digits, such as COSC 220 or MATH241.
constraints: Do not validate against the catalog, only the shape.
hints: Ignore one space if it appears between the letters and numbers.
After removing that space, the code should have exactly 7 characters.
Check that the first 4 characters are uppercase letters and the last 3 are digits.

questions.title: Find Index
questions.prompt: Return the index of the first occurrence of a target value in a list, or -1 if it is absent.
hints: Loop over indexes, not only values.
Compare each value with the target.
Return immediately when found.

questions.title: Merge Names
questions.prompt: Given two lists of names, return one list containing all names from the first list followed by all names from the second.
hints: Create a result list.
Add every item from the first list.
Then add every item from the second list.

questions.title: Temperature Above Threshold
questions.prompt: Count how many temperature readings are strictly greater than a threshold.
hints: Initialize a counter.
Compare each reading with the threshold.
Increment only for readings above it.

visualizer.title: Temperature Above Threshold: compare each reading
visualizer.caption: Watch each temperature get compared with the threshold before the count changes.

questions.title: Last Digit
questions.prompt: Given a non-negative integer n, return only its last digit as an integer. For example, 384 should return 4.
hints: The last digit is the remainder after dividing by 10.
Use n % 10 to get that remainder.
Check n = 0 too; its last digit should still be 0.

questions.title: Truthy Attendance
questions.prompt: Given a list of booleans for attendance, count how many values are true.
hints: Start a counter at zero.
Check each value directly.
Increment for true values.

questions.title: Initials
questions.prompt: Given a full name, return the uppercase initials of each word.
hints: Split into words.
Take the first character of each word.
Uppercase the collected initials.

questions.title: Clamp Score
questions.prompt: Clamp a score so values below 0 become 0 and values above 100 become 100.
hints: Check the lower bound.
Check the upper bound.
Return the original score when it is inside range.

questions.title: Every Other Item
questions.prompt: Return a new list containing every other item from the input, starting at index 0.
hints: Loop indexes by 2.
Start at index 0.
Append the selected values to a result list.

questions.title: Count Digits
questions.prompt: Return how many digits are in a non-negative integer. For 0, return 1.
hints: Start with the special case: 0 has one digit.
For any other number, remove the last digit by dividing by 10 and keeping the whole-number part.
Count each removal until the number becomes 0.

questions.title: Matrix Column Sums
questions.prompt: Given a rectangular matrix of integers, return a list with the sum of each column.
constraints: All non-empty rows have the same length.
hints: If the matrix has no rows, return an empty list right away.
Use the first row to know how many column totals you need.
For each row, add row[0] to column total 0, row[1] to column total 1, and so on.

questions.title: Can Vote
questions.prompt: Return true if an age is at least 18, otherwise return false.
hints: The cutoff is inclusive, so age 18 should return true.
Compare the age with 18 using greater-than-or-equal.
Return the result of that comparison instead of writing extra branches.

questions.title: Unique Count
questions.prompt: Given a list of integers, return how many different values appear at least once. Repeated values should only count one time.
hints: Use a set because it stores one copy of each value.
Add each number from the list into the set.
The answer is the number of items left in the set.

questions.title: Plant Watering Message
questions.prompt: A student is tracking a classroom plant. Given the soil moisture reading and whether the window is sunny today, return the care message for the plant.
constraints: Moisture is an integer from 0 to 100.
Return exactly water today or check tomorrow.
hints: Very low moisture means the plant needs water.
Sunny days dry the plant faster, so use a higher moisture cutoff when it is sunny.
Return one of the two exact messages from the prompt.

questions.title: Temperature Comfort Count
questions.prompt: Given hourly room temperature readings and an inclusive comfort range, count how many readings are comfortable.
constraints: The readings list may be empty.
hints: Start a counter at zero.
Check both the low and high limit for each reading.
Increment only when the reading is inside the inclusive range.

questions.title: Grocery Price Lookup
questions.prompt: A grocery list stores item names next to their prices. Given parallel lists of item names and prices plus a target item, return the target price or -1 if the item is not listed.
constraints: items and prices have the same length.
hints: Match each item name with the price at the same index.
Compare each item name with the target.
Return -1 only after checking every item.

questions.title: Course Credit Total
questions.prompt: Given course names, their credit values, and a list of selected courses, return the total number of credits for the selected courses. Ignore selected names that are not in the course list.
constraints: courses and credits have the same length.
A selected course that is missing from courses contributes 0 credits.
hints: Build a lookup from course name to credit value, or scan the course list for each selection.
Start the total at zero.
Add credits only for selected courses that exist in the course list.

questions.title: Favorite Course Counts
questions.prompt: Students voted for their favorite course topic. Given all votes and a list of target topics, return how many votes each target topic received, in target order.
constraints: Targets may include topics with zero votes.
Return counts in the same order as targets.
hints: Count how often each favorite appears.
Create one answer for each target topic.
Use zero when a target topic never appeared.

questions.title: Unique Parking Zones
questions.prompt: Given a list of parking zone labels seen on campus, return how many different zones appear. Repeated zones should count once.
constraints: The zone list may be empty.
hints: A set keeps one copy of each zone.
Add every zone label to the set.
Return the size of the set.

questions.title: Shared Study Topics
questions.prompt: Two students list the topics they want to review. Return the topics that appear in both lists, keeping the order from the first student and avoiding duplicates.
constraints: Do not repeat a shared topic in the result.
hints: Put the second student's topics in a set for fast lookup.
Scan the first student's list from left to right.
Append a topic only if it is shared and not already in the result.

questions.title: Pair Names With Scores
questions.prompt: Given parallel lists of student names and scores, return a list of name-score pairs written as name:score strings.
constraints: names and scores have the same length.
hints: Loop over indexes so each name lines up with its score.
Convert each score to text before joining it with the name.
Append each name:score string to the result list.

questions.title: Swap Pair Order
questions.prompt: Given a two-item pair represented as a list of strings, return a new pair with the two items swapped. If fewer than two items are provided, return the pair unchanged.
constraints: The input list has 0, 1, or 2 strings.
Do not mutate the original pair.
hints: Check whether the pair has at least two items.
If it does, return the second item followed by the first.
Otherwise return a copy of the original pair.

questions.title: Late Assignment Penalty
questions.prompt: Given an assignment score and the number of days it was submitted late, subtract 5 points per late day and return the final score. The final score cannot be below zero.
hints: Compute the penalty as daysLate times 5.
Subtract the penalty from the score.
If the result is below zero, return zero instead.

questions.title: Weekly Plant Care Days
questions.prompt: A student records plant moisture readings for a week starting on Monday. Given the readings and a watering threshold, return the day names where the plant should be watered.
constraints: Readings are in weekday order starting with Monday.
Only the first seven readings need weekday names.
hints: Store the weekday names in order.
Loop over the readings by index.
When a reading is below the threshold, append the matching weekday name.

questions.title: Max Plate Stack Height
questions.prompt: A dining hall records stack commands: push adds one plate and pop removes one plate if any are present. Return the highest stack height reached.
constraints: Pop on an empty stack leaves it empty.
hints: Track the current stack height.
Increase it for push and decrease it for pop only when positive.
Keep the largest height seen after each command.

visualizer.title: Plate Stack: push and pop height
visualizer.caption: Watch the stack grow and shrink while the maximum height is remembered.

questions.title: Serve First Students
questions.prompt: Students line up for tutoring help. Given the queue of names and a number to serve, return the names served from the front of the queue.
constraints: serveCount may be larger than the queue length.
Keep the original queue order for served students.
hints: A queue serves the oldest waiting student first.
Take names from the front until serveCount is reached or the queue is empty.
Append each served name to the result list.

visualizer.title: Tutoring Queue: serve from the front
visualizer.caption: Watch students leave in the same order they joined.

questions.title: First Score At Least
questions.prompt: Given sorted quiz scores and a target score, return the first index whose score is at least the target. Return -1 if every score is lower.
hints: You are looking for the first score that is not too small.
A linear scan is fine for the beginner version.
Return as soon as you find a score greater than or equal to the target.

visualizer.title: First At Least: find the boundary
visualizer.caption: Watch the boundary between too-small scores and acceptable scores.

questions.title: Countdown List
questions.prompt: Return a countdown list from n down to 0. If n is negative, return an empty list.
hints: A recursive version stops when n is below zero.
Add the current number first.
Then continue with n - 1 until reaching zero.

visualizer.title: Countdown: smaller call each time
visualizer.caption: Watch each call ask for the rest of the countdown.

questions.title: Follow Linked List Values
questions.prompt: A linked list is represented by values, nextIndexes, and a head index. Follow next indexes from head and return the values in order. A next index of -1 means the end.
constraints: The list has no cycle in this beginner version.
hints: Start at the head index.
Append the value at the current index.
Move to nextIndexes[current] until it becomes -1.

visualizer.title: Follow next links
visualizer.caption: Watch the current index move from node to node.

questions.title: Edge Pair Matches
questions.prompt: Count how many outside-in word pairs match as you move from the edges of a list toward the middle.
constraints: Move left forward and right backward after each comparison.
Do not compare the middle item with itself.
hints: Start one pointer at the first word and one at the last word.
If the two words match, add 1 to the count.
Stop when the left pointer is no longer before the right pointer.

visualizer.title: Edge Pairs: compare both ends
visualizer.caption: Watch two pointers move inward one pair at a time.

questions.title: Count Short Study Blocks
questions.prompt: Count how many two-session study windows fit within a time limit.
constraints: A window is exactly two neighboring sessions.
Count a window when the two values add up to limit or less.
A list with fewer than two sessions returns 0.
hints: Start with the sum of minutes[0] and minutes[1].
Slide one position at a time to check the next pair.
Increase the count whenever the current pair is short enough.

visualizer.title: Two-Session Window
visualizer.caption: Watch a fixed-size window slide across adjacent sessions.

questions.title: Recursive Factorial Small
questions.prompt: Return n factorial using a recursive idea for a small non-negative number.
constraints: For n greater than 1, multiply n by the factorial of n - 1.
hints: Write the stopping case before the recursive case.
The stopping case is n <= 1.
The recursive case multiplies n by the answer for n - 1.

visualizer.title: Factorial: multiply on return
visualizer.caption: Watch calls shrink down to 1, then multiply while returning.
